Devengo vs. caja rule
nodes.rationale: Spanish IVA/IRPF settle on the fecha de devengo (issue date), not collection date. BudgetGuard books income on collection (cash basis), which is wrong for every tax model, so a dedicated accrual view exists and is the only legal entry point for fiscal computations. Verified against a real rectificativa (CREST-01, 600,00 EUR) that had to be filed because a human overrode the correct accrual figure with the bank-statement date.

nodes.label: Cross-quarter alert (warns, does not fix)
nodes.rationale: The figures were never wrong; the failure was a human reasoning from the bank statement instead of the accrual view. So the feature deliberately warns a human and changes no total, no casilla, no deadline. Four disagreement cases are classified, one of which (declared-in-earlier-period with a lost link) can never be fully recovered because there is no collection date to compare.

nodes.label: Asymmetric fiscal filter (income vs expense)
nodes.rationale: All paid income enters the fiscal view (professional status decided later by category), but an expense only enters once fiscally coded. Making this filter symmetric once erased 44.954 EUR of uncoded 2023 invoices from the 130, 390 and 100 of that year.

nodes.label: The two deduction shares (IRPF vs IVA)
nodes.rationale: A coded expense answers two different articles: DeductionPercent (art. 30.2.5.a LIRPF, IRPF share) and VatDeductionPercent (art. 95 LIVA, input-VAT share) can legitimately diverge on the same receipt (7.5% vs 0% on home-office supplies). A single column previously deducted input VAT a comprobacion would disallow. NULL means 'inherit the IRPF share', never 0, resolved once in SQL via COALESCE so no model can forget the rule and no already-filed casilla 29 is silently zeroed.

nodes.label: IVA a compensar: the pool
nodes.rationale: With no output VAT (all-abroad clients), input VAT never offsets anything and accumulates. The opening balance is stored, not recomputed, because a recomputation would disagree with AEAT's own registry; compensation quotas expire after four years (art. 99.5 LIVA), and 139,15 EUR was found to have already expired unnoticed on this user's real pool.

nodes.label: Creditos incobrables (art. 80.Cuatro LIVA)
nodes.rationale: The module is a clock and checklist only -- it issues no rectificativa and files no modelo 952. It is fail-closed: an invoice enters only when it has a cuota repercutida > 0 AND an established recipient, on two independent legal grounds (no cuota to recover under operaciones no sujetas; art. 80.Cinco.2.a excludes non-established recipients). For this taxpayer's foreign-client portfolio the tracked list is correctly empty; excluded invoices carry their exclusion reason instead of vanishing, so the module does not read as broken.

nodes.label: Modelo 390 casilla 97 vs 662 / 108 vs 110 split
nodes.rationale: Casilla 97 must carry only the last period's own a-compensar result (what AEAT reconciles against the 4T 303); putting the annual aggregate there mismatched the 4T 303 and would trigger a requerimiento. Casilla 108 (total volumen de operaciones) must be the sum of domestic + non-subject bases; setting 108 = 110 zeroed the volumen the day a single domestic invoice appeared -- a golden-master test pins 108 = 110 + domestic base.

nodes.label: An official form proves only its own campaign
nodes.rationale: The ejercicio 2023 Modelo 100 form has no casilla 0196, but the filed 2025 Renta does (RETA regularisation). Reading the 2023 form as authoritative for 2025 led to deleting a box that actually exists. Authority for a filed year is a filed modelo of that year, not an older reference form.

nodes.label: Amortizacion del inmovilizado
nodes.rationale: An asset is not consumed in its purchase year (art. 30.2 RIRPF, tabla de amortizacion simplificada). Until this module existed the whole purchase was deducted in the purchase year, which required a real Renta rectification (Lenovo laptop, 869 EUR). The rate is stored on the asset, never re-derived from its group, because the tabla is a maximum, the ERD doubling depends on facts the group can't express, and a recomputed rate at read time would rewrite an already-filed dotacion.

nodes.label: Asset double-deduction guard (link required, never zero DeductionPercent)
nodes.rationale: An asset's purchase must be excluded from IRPF models (Modelo 130/100/projection) once it is registered, or the same laptop is deducted twice -- once as a period expense and once as the dotacion. Exclusion happens at read time via getAssetTransactionIds(), not by zeroing DeductionPercent, because zeroing would also erase the purchase's input VAT from Modelo 303/390 (only avoidable now that the two deduction shares are split) and because it does not survive the link being undone (ON DELETE SET NULL). A missing link is surfaced (UnlinkedPurchaseNotice) and a candidate purchase suggested but never auto-linked, because a wrong link is worse than no link.

nodes.label: Aplazamientos y fraccionamientos
nodes.rationale: An AEAT deferral instalment bundles three legally different items paid together: principal (the tax itself, not an expense), recargo de apremio (never deductible, art. 15.c LIS) and interes de demora (a deductible financial expense, casilla 0203). Before this module, instalments were typed in whole as pending expenses, which both hid deductible interest and wrongly deducted the tax itself. The split (ANEXO I) is read from the letter, never derived by dividing the total, because AEAT loads the rounding remainder onto the last fraccion.

nodes.label: Deferral cancellation: guard in the UPDATE, not a pre-check
nodes.rationale: Only rows still 'pending' are matched by the UPDATE that cancels a fraccion, so a fraccion marked paid between confirmation and click is never rewritten, and two racing cancellations cannot both claim the same fraccion -- the second gets a 409 conflict. Paid movements are left exactly as they are because that money really left the account and its interes remains a deductible expense of the year it was paid. The Deferrals row itself is never deleted, because deleting it would free the UNIQUE(UserID, ExpedienteNumber) constraint and let a re-upload silently re-book cancelled instalments.

nodes.label: The IRPF provision
nodes.rationale: Modelo 130 pays a flat 20% of net income while the Renta charges a progressive scale; the difference arrives as one payment the following June. The projection composes pure helpers, extrapolating year-to-date figures by run-rate, applying the state+regional (Madrid) scale, and relieving the minimo personal against the gross quota rather than subtracting it from the base. Amortization is deliberately excluded from the run-rate and subtracted as a full-year figure, or January would inflate the projected dotacion roughly thirtyfold.

nodes.label: Year-keyed lookup, never edited in place (ley-set figures)
nodes.rationale: IRPF_YEAR_FIGURES mirrors the shape of RENTA_WINDOWS deliberately: a date or amount set by ley cannot be derived from the previous year's, only looked up, and a missing year falls back to the last published figure labelled as provisional rather than presented as fact. While the figures were flat constants, updating them for a new ley rewrote the projection of every year already declared.

nodes.label: Pension contributions (arts. 51-52 Ley 35/2006)
nodes.rationale: Pension contributions reduce the base imponible general (not an expense, ignored entirely by Modelo 130 per art. 110 RIRPF). Two buckets are stored separately -- individual (1.500 EUR ceiling) and employment (+4.250 EUR increment, only for planes de empleo simplificados) -- because a single stored total could not be validated: 5.750 EUR is legal as 1.500+4.250 but illegal as 5.750 in an individual plan alone. The 30% cap applies to the sum, not either bucket; an earlier implementation clamped the 1.500 against the individual bucket alone and a unit test encoded that bug with a misleadingly authoritative comment.

nodes.label: Deadlines (local time, carry-over)
nodes.rationale: A deadline is a calendar day in Spain, so all dates are computed in local time -- reading them in UTC once moved 30 January 2027 to a Friday. Every period is filed in the year after it (10 January files Q4's 303/130/390 and the previous year's Renta runs April-June), so a surface computing only the current calendar year finds everything not_due on exactly the days something is owed. getCarryOverDeadlines() fixes this purely, never inventing a deadline: it filters what computeDeadlines() already emits for a closed year down to windows still open (upcoming/due only, never overdue).
